world.canon: Luke-scoped resurrection dawn. The women are the SAME group of first-century Judean women throughout (Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and others) in plain wool tunics with mantles drawn over the head, muted natural dyes, sandals. The tomb is HEWN IN STONE and new (Luke 23:53), a low rock-cut opening in a garden, its great round stone rolled aside. The two heavenly witnesses are MEN in dazzling shining white garments, radiant with light, WITHOUT wings (Luke 24:4, 'two men'). NO Roman guards at the women's dawn tomb (Matthew-only). Where the risen Christ shows wounds, they are in the HANDS and FEET (Luke 24:39-40), never the pierced side.
